title: Analyse Your Trading Statement with Claude AI
subtitle: A beginner's guide to turning your broker's trade report into clear answers: profit and loss, win rate, best and worst trades, and what to improve. No spreadsheet skills needed.
footer: Trading Statement Analysis with Claude: A Beginner's Guide
info: A Claude account (claude.ai or the Claude app) and your trade report file
CSV, Excel (XLSX) or PDF statements from your broker
Works on the free plan for small reports. Paid plans give more usage for big files and long chats.
About 10 minutes for your first analysis
Educational guide only, not financial or tax advice

sections.h1: 1. What can Claude do with your statement?

sections.p: Your broker gives you a tradebook (every buy and sell) and a P&L report (profit and loss). They are long tables that are hard to read. You upload the file to Claude and ask questions in plain English (or Tamil). Claude reads the data, runs real calculations with code, and explains the results, often with charts.

table: Total, by month, by stock or instrument, and gross vs after charges
How many trades made money vs lost money, as a percentage
Your biggest wins and losses, and what they had in common
Average win vs average loss, profit factor, longest losing streak, biggest drop
Patterns like over-trading, holding losers too long, or one setup losing money

bullets: Good fit: intraday, F&O and swing traders who want to understand their own results without building spreadsheets.
Good fit: investors who want a simple summary of a year of trades.
Not for: getting buy or sell tips. Claude analyses your past trades. It can't predict the market.
Not a replacement for your broker's official tax P&L or a chartered accountant at tax time.

sections.p: Every broker has a reports section. Download the tradebook for the period you want, as Excel (XLSX) or CSV if possible. Those are easier for Claude to calculate from than PDF.

table: Console > Reports > Tradebook (choose segment and dates, then download XLSX or CSV). P&L is under Reports > P&L.
Look for Reports, Statements or Tradebook in the web or app menu. Choose a date range and export to Excel or CSV.

sections.small: Zerodha itself advises checking its P&L report against the tradebook and contract notes, because reports are prepared from the data available when you generate them.

sections.callout: Before uploading, open the file and delete or blank out your name, client ID, PAN, phone number, email, bank details and address. Claude only needs the trade rows: date, symbol, buy/sell, quantity, price and charges. Save it as a new file, e.g. trades_clean.xlsx.
sections.title: Protect your data first

bullets: Check your Claude privacy setting: Settings > Privacy > "Help improve Claude". Turn it off if you don't want your chats used to train future models.
Use an incognito chat for sensitive files. Anthropic says incognito chats aren't used to improve Claude.
Open claude.ai (or the app) and start a new chat.
For Excel files, make sure Claude's code execution / file creation feature is turned on in Settings (it's needed to read and calculate XLSX files).
Click the + or paperclip button, attach your cleaned file, and paste the prompt below.

sections.code:
I'm a trader in India. Attached is my tradebook for [period].
Please analyse it and give me:
1. Total profit/loss, gross and after charges, and by month
2. Win rate: number of winning vs losing trades
3. My 5 best and 5 worst trades, and what they have in common
4. Average win vs average loss, profit factor, longest losing streak
5. P&L by stock/instrument and by day of the week
6. 3 specific areas I should improve, based only on this data
Show your calculations, list any rows you couldn't read,
and make simple charts. Don't give buy/sell recommendations.

sections.p: Claude matches buys with sells to work out each trade's result. If your file has odd column names, it will ask or explain what it assumed. Read that part.

table: "How much did brokerage, STT and other charges cost me in total?"
Charges quietly eat profits, especially in frequent intraday trading
"Do I lose more on trades held past my usual exit?"
"Which time of day or weekday is my worst?"
"What happened after a big loss: did I trade more?"
"Make a one-page summary I can save"
Gives you a report to compare month by month

bullets: Double-check the totals. Compare Claude's total P&L with your broker's P&L report. If they differ, ask Claude why (missing rows, charges or open positions are common reasons).
PDF statements are less reliable than Excel or CSV, because tables can get split across pages. Use XLSX or CSV whenever you can.
Very large files may hit upload or usage limits. Split by quarter or month, or upload CSV instead of a big Excel file.
It's analysis, not advice. Claude can show patterns in your past trades. It doesn't know the future, and it isn't a SEBI-registered adviser.
For tax filing, use your broker's Tax P&L report and a chartered accountant. Claude can help you understand it, but don't file from its numbers alone.

table: Broker reports > Tradebook > download XLSX or CSV
Delete name, PAN, client ID and bank details; use an incognito chat
Upload the file to Claude and paste the prompt from section 5
Compare Claude's total with your broker's P&L report
Ask about worst trades, weekdays, holding time and charges
Repeat every month with the same prompt and compare summaries
